title_primary: Local demographic reorganization does not imply a transferable island-resilience rule in Antarctic penguins
title_alternative: Local island reorganization does not yield a transferable demographic rule across Antarctic penguin populations
fit_rationale: The manuscript links biological organization to geography at nested local-to-continental scales.
The core conceptual contribution is a boundary on transferability: ecological information can be strong within islands without moving reliably through static island descriptors across populations.

A prospectively frozen Signy transfer test independently shows that a locally informative Palmer dynamic correlate also fails primary replication, strengthening the information-transfer framing without replacing the two core tests.
The Antarctic-wide component compares three Pygoscelis species while Palmer provides the discovery system and Signy provides a bounded independent transfer test.
Title wording uses 'does not imply' rather than an absence claim because moderate common Antarctic-wide effects remain unresolved by the MDE analysis.
editorial_risk: The Antarctic-wide primary result is non-confirmatory; editors may ask whether the manuscript is sufficiently biogeographical rather than demographic.
The Palmer dynamic result is fixed-specification and the Signy primary replication is null; these must reinforce transferability boundaries rather than create a third positive claim.
Do not oversell radius variation as scale dependence; joint null p=0.0810.
Do not imply absence of moderate effects; MDE80/MDE90 indicate low sensitivity near the observed interaction magnitude.
cover_letter_angle: The paper uses nested discovery, replication and continental tests to distinguish local island information from information that transfers across island systems. Palmer concentration is strong; a local dynamic correlate fails frozen Signy replication; and static Antarctic-wide island architecture does not yield a confirmed general coupling rule.
prohibited_pitch: A positive option-fragmentation crossover was discovered.
The study proves island architecture does not matter.
The 5 km sign reversal demonstrates ecological scale dependence.
The Palmer dynamic signal is a general win-stay/lose-switch mechanism.
Signy independently replicated the Palmer lag-2 signal.
The species-wide latent factor is an identified climate mechanism.
